convertedTask.title: Set up AWS Site-to-Site VPN and verify routes
convertedTask.goal: Goal: Create a Site-to-Site VPN to an on-prem router and verify route behaviour.

concepts.title: Customer Gateway
concepts.body: Represents the on-prem router in AWS.

concepts.title: Virtual Private Gateway
concepts.body: The AWS-side VPN gateway attached to one VPC.

concepts.title: VPN route plan
concepts.body: SideCIDRRoute targetReasonVPC192.168.10.0/24vgwSend on-prem traffic to VPNOn-prem10.70.0.0/16VPN tunnelSend VPC traffic to AWSTunnelTwo IPsec tunnelsBGP or staticHigh availability path

convertedTask.whyItMatters: This matters because hybrid networking needs routing on both sides. AWS can build the VPN, but the router must also send return traffic back.

values.label: Required permissions summary
values.value: STS identity check, VPC networking changes, related service setup, verification, and cleanup for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM user, IAM role, or IAM Identity Center permission set.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with VPC permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with VPC permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity VPN setup: ec2:CreateCustomerGateway, ec2:CreateVpnGateway, ec2:AttachVpnGateway, ec2:CreateVpnConnection, ec2:DescribeVpnConnections Routing: ec2:CreateRoute, ec2:ReplaceRoute, ec2:DescribeRouteTables Cleanup: ec2:DeleteVpnConnection, ec2:DetachVpnGateway, ec2:DeleteVpnGateway, ec2:DeleteCustomerGateway
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Create the Customer Gateway

instructions.text: Open VPC → Customer gateways.
Choose Create customer gateway.
Name: saa-vpc-task17-cgw.
Routing: choose Static for a simple lab, or Dynamic if your router supports BGP.
IP address: enter your on-prem router public IP.

consoleSteps.warning: Use a real static public IP for a real VPN. The placeholder IP will not form a tunnel.

consoleSteps.title: Create and attach the Virtual Private Gateway

instructions.text: Open VPC → Virtual private gateways.
Choose Create virtual private gateway.
Name: saa-vpc-task17-vgw.
ASN: use Amazon default ASN for this lab.
Select the new gateway, choose Actions → Attach to VPC.

consoleSteps.title: Create the Site-to-Site VPN connection

instructions.text: Open VPC → Site-to-Site VPN connections.
Choose Create VPN connection.
Target gateway type: Virtual private gateway.
Customer gateway: choose saa-vpc-task17-cgw.
Routing options: choose Static and add 192.168.10.0/24.

consoleSteps.note: Download the router configuration for your router vendor after creation.

consoleSteps.title: Update VPC route tables

instructions.text: Open VPC → Route tables.
Select the private subnet route table.
Choose Routes → Edit routes.
Add destination 192.168.10.0/24 and target the virtual private gateway.

consoleSteps.note: The return route must also exist on the on-prem router.

consoleSteps.title: Verify tunnel and routes

instructions.text: Open the VPN connection.
Check Tunnel details.
Look for tunnel status UP after router configuration.
Ping or connect from an allowed private EC2 instance to an on-prem test IP.

consoleSteps.warning: Security groups, NACLs, firewalls, and the on-prem router must all allow the test traffic.

instructions.text: Delete the VPN connection.
Remove route table routes to the on-prem CIDR.
Detach the virtual private gateway from the VPC.
Delete the virtual private gateway.
Delete the customer gateway.

cliSteps.title: Check your AWS identity
cliSteps.note: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: you see your AWS account ID and ARN.

cliSteps.title: Create Customer Gateway

commands.text:
CGW_ID=$(aws ec2 create-customer-gateway --region $REGION --type ipsec.1 --public-ip $CGW_IP --bgp-asn 65000 --query 'CustomerGateway.CustomerGatewayId' --output text)
echo $CGW_ID

cliSteps.warning: Use a real router public IP for a working tunnel.

cliSteps.title: Create and attach Virtual Private Gateway

commands.text:
VGW_ID=$(aws ec2 create-vpn-gateway --region $REGION --type ipsec.1 --query 'VpnGateway.VpnGatewayId' --output text)
aws ec2 attach-vpn-gateway --region $REGION --vpn-gateway-id $VGW_ID --vpc-id $VPC_ID
echo $VGW_ID

cliSteps.note: Wait until attached before creating the VPN.

cliSteps.title: Create VPN connection with static route

commands.text:
VPN_ID=$(aws ec2 create-vpn-connection --region $REGION --type ipsec.1 --customer-gateway-id $CGW_ID --vpn-gateway-id $VGW_ID --options StaticRoutesOnly=true --query 'VpnConnection.VpnConnectionId' --output text)
aws ec2 create-vpn-connection-route --region $REGION --vpn-connection-id $VPN_ID --destination-cidr-block $ONPREM_CIDR
echo $VPN_ID

cliSteps.note: Expected: VPN connection is created with two tunnels.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: VPN connection is created with two tunnels.

cliSteps.title: Add VPC route
cliSteps.note: Expected: route target is the VGW.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: route target is the VGW.

cliSteps.title: Check VPN state
cliSteps.note: Expected after router setup: at least one tunnel is UP.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected after router setup: at least one tunnel is UP.

cliSteps.title: Cleanup VPN resources

commands.text:
aws ec2 delete-vpn-connection --region $REGION --vpn-connection-id $VPN_ID
aws ec2 detach-vpn-gateway --region $REGION --vpn-gateway-id $VGW_ID --vpc-id $VPC_ID
aws ec2 delete-vpn-gateway --region $REGION --vpn-gateway-id $VGW_ID
aws ec2 delete-customer-gateway --region $REGION --customer-gateway-id $CGW_ID

cliSteps.warning: Remove route table entries if they remain.

verification.text: Virtual Private Cloud configuration verified in Amazon VPC.

cleanup.text: Delete subnets, route tables, Internet Gateways, and the custom VPC created during this lab.
Release the Elastic IP address to prevent unattached public IPv4 hourly charges.

cheatSheet.title: VPN route checklist
cheatSheet.body: CheckAWS sideOn-prem sideVPC CIDR10.70.0.0/16Route back to AWSOn-prem CIDRRoute to vgwLocal networkSecuritySG/NACL allow trafficFirewall allows trafficTunnelTelemetry UPIPsec configured

troubleshooting.title: Tunnel is DOWN
troubleshooting.body: Check pre-shared key, public IP, IKE/IPsec settings, and router NAT/firewall rules.

troubleshooting.title: Tunnel is UP but traffic fails
troubleshooting.body: Check routes in both directions, security groups, NACLs, and on-prem firewalls.

troubleshooting.title: Static route missing
troubleshooting.body: For static VPN, add the on-prem CIDR to the VPN connection and the VPC route table.

examTraps.title: AWS VPN has two tunnels
examTraps.body: Use both tunnels for high availability.

examTraps.title: Return route is required
examTraps.body: A VPC route alone is not enough. The on-prem network must route back.

examTraps.title: Static vs BGP
examTraps.body: Static routes are manually added. BGP advertises routes dynamically.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Understand Virtual Private Cloud configuration and architectural best practices in Amazon VPC.

convertedTask.title: Create a Direct Connect private VIF and test VPC routing
convertedTask.goal: Goal: Create a private virtual interface for Direct Connect and route private traffic to a VPC.

concepts.title: Private VIF
concepts.body: A private virtual interface connects Direct Connect to private AWS resources through a VGW or Direct Connect gateway.

concepts.title: Direct Connect gateway
concepts.body: A Direct Connect gateway can connect a private VIF to one or more VPCs through gateway associations.

concepts.title: Direct Connect route plan
concepts.body: ItemExamplePurposeCost riskConnectiondxcon-...Physical or hosted DX linkHighPrivate VIFVLAN + BGP peerPrivate AWS routingMediumDX gatewaysaa-vpc-task19-dxgwConnect VIF to VGWLowVGWAttached to VPCVPC-side gatewayLow

convertedTask.whyItMatters: This matters because Direct Connect is private dedicated connectivity. It is not encrypted by default and is different from VPN over the internet.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with an IAM user, IAM role, or IAM Identity Center permission set.

Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with VPC permissions.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity Direct Connect read: directconnect:DescribeConnections, directconnect:DescribeVirtualInterfaces, directconnect:DescribeDirectConnectGateways Direct Connect setup: directconnect:CreatePrivateVirtualInterface, directconnect:CreateDirectConnectGateway, directconnect:CreateDirectConnectGatewayAssociation, directconnect:DeleteVirtualInterface VPC gateway and routes: ec2:CreateVpnGateway, ec2:AttachVpnGateway, ec2:CreateRoute, ec2:DescribeRouteTables Cleanup: directconnect:DeleteDirectConnectGatewayAssociation, directconnect:DeleteDirectConnectGateway, ec2:DetachVpnGateway, ec2:DeleteVpnGateway

consoleSteps.title: Confirm you have a Direct Connect connection

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect.
Choose Connections.
Confirm an active dedicated or hosted connection exists.
Do not create paid Direct Connect resources unless this is a real lab account.

consoleSteps.warning: This task cannot fully work without an existing Direct Connect connection and on-prem router setup.

consoleSteps.title: Create a Direct Connect gateway

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect → Direct Connect gateways.
Choose Create Direct Connect gateway.
Name: saa-vpc-task19-dxgw.
Amazon-side ASN: use 64512 for this example.

consoleSteps.note: Use an ASN that does not conflict with your network.

consoleSteps.title: Create or confirm the VPC Virtual Private Gateway

instructions.text: Open VPC → Virtual private gateways.
Create saa-vpc-task19-vgw if needed.
Attach it to the lab VPC.
Associate the VGW with the Direct Connect gateway.

consoleSteps.note: Allowed prefixes should include the VPC CIDR.

consoleSteps.title: Create the private virtual interface

instructions.text: Open Direct Connect → Virtual interfaces.
Choose Create virtual interface.
Type: Private.
Connection: choose the active connection.
Gateway: choose the Direct Connect gateway.
Enter VLAN, BGP ASN, and peer IPs from your network plan.

consoleSteps.warning: Wrong VLAN or BGP peer values stop routing from working.

consoleSteps.title: Update route tables and test

instructions.text: Open VPC → Route tables.
Add the on-prem CIDR route to the VGW if needed.
Confirm BGP routes are advertised on the router.
Test private IP traffic between on-prem and a private EC2 instance.

consoleSteps.note: Security groups and on-prem firewalls must allow the test traffic.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down in dependency order

instructions.text: Delete or disable the private VIF if created for a lab.
Delete the Direct Connect gateway association.
Delete the Direct Connect gateway if created for a lab.
Remove VPC routes to on-prem.
Detach and delete the VGW if created for this lab.

consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete production Direct Connect resources.

cliSteps.title: Template private VIF command

commands.text:
cat > private-vif.json <<'EOF'
{
  "virtualInterfaceName": "saa-vpc-task19-private-vif",
  "vlan": 101,
  "asn": 65000,
  "authKey": "CHANGE-ME",
  "amazonAddress": "169.254.100.1/30",
  "customerAddress": "169.254.100.2/30",
  "addressFamily": "ipv4",
  "directConnectGatewayId": "REPLACE-DXGW-ID"
}
EOF
aws directconnect create-private-virtual-interface --region $REGION --connection-id $DX_CONNECTION_ID --new-private-virtual-interface file://private-vif.json

cliSteps.warning: Edit the JSON with real VLAN, ASN, BGP key, peer IPs, and DXGW ID before running.

cliSteps.title: Verify VIF state
cliSteps.note: Expected: VIF eventually becomes available when accepted/configured.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: VIF eventually becomes available when accepted/configured.

commands.text:
# Replace with the VIF ID created for this lab only
VIF_ID=dxvif-xxxxxxxx
aws directconnect delete-virtual-interface --region $REGION --virtual-interface-id $VIF_ID

cliSteps.warning: Do not delete shared or production Direct Connect resources.

troubleshooting.title: No Direct Connect connection
troubleshooting.body: You cannot create a working private VIF without an active dedicated or hosted connection.

troubleshooting.title: BGP down
troubleshooting.body: Check VLAN, ASN, BGP auth key, and peer IP addresses.

troubleshooting.title: Traffic still fails
troubleshooting.body: Check VPC routes, allowed prefixes, security groups, NACLs, and on-prem firewall rules.

examTraps.title: Direct Connect is not encrypted by default
examTraps.body: Use VPN over Direct Connect or app encryption if encryption is required.

examTraps.title: Private VIF is for private resources
examTraps.body: Use private VIF for VPC private connectivity, not public AWS service endpoints.

examTraps.title: Transit VIF differs from private VIF
examTraps.body: Transit VIF is used with Transit Gateway through a Direct Connect gateway.
